# Core CRM, CMS and database — implementation record

**Purpose.** This is the one execution record for building the plan in [`core-crm-cms-database-target-architecture.md`](./core-crm-cms-database-target-architecture.md) ("the plan"). It says what is being built, by whom, in what order, what has been integrated and what has been verified. Another agent can resume the work from this file alone.

**Who edits it.** Only the coordinating agent edits this file. Delegates report in their handoffs, and the coordinator records what it has checked. A delegate's report that work is finished is recorded as _implemented_. It becomes _integrated_ when the coordinator has merged it, and _verified_ only when the coordinator has seen the evidence on the integrated revision.

**Tracking issue:** [#2671](https://github.com/Asymmetric-al/core/issues/2671). Each package has its own issue, listed in section 5.

## 3. Working rules for every delegate

1. **Read first.** The root `AGENTS.md`, the nearest nested `AGENTS.md`, the rulebooks that match the work, and the plan sections the brief names. The package's acceptance list in section 12 of the plan is normative. Current source, tests and manifests decide what exists.
2. **Stay in scope.** Edit only what the brief assigns. A needed change outside it is reported in the handoff, not made. Requirements, acceptance criteria, tests and gates are never weakened to make work pass.
3. **Test first.** Behaviour changes use red, green, refactor at the nearest stable seam. Each defect or rule gets a test that fails before the change and passes after it.
4. **Migrations.** Create each file with `bun run supabase -- migration new <name>`. Do not refer to a migration by its timestamp anywhere else. The coordinator settles the final order at integration.
5. **Databases.** Use the shared test Postgres with your own database names. `DATABASE_URL=<url> node scripts/verify/supabase-migrations.mjs` applies the migration chain and runs the catalog and field-policy gates. Real-stack suites take the same URL as `TENANT_GUARD_IT_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL`. Never point a command at a hosted project. A role, its memberships and its password belong to the whole cluster, not to one database: on the shared test Postgres create no role, grant no membership in `cms_owner` or `cms_runtime`, and never alter those two roles. Work that connects as them, or needs a login role of its own, runs on a Postgres that is yours alone: an assigned stack slot, or a container of your own on a port in your slot's range (D-34).
6. **Never.** Push, open a pull request, bypass a hook, commit a secret, run `supabase start` or `cms:local:*` on the default ports, stop a container you did not start, or edit this record.
7. **Commit.** Small Conventional Commits on the branch the brief names, `type(AL-<issue>): subject`.
8. **Hand off** with: what changed and which plan lines it satisfies; the branch and commit hashes; each check run with its result; environment assumptions; failures, limits and unfinished work; and what the change means for migrations and documentation.
9. **Credentials.** A brief names the one `core-env` profile a task needs, or none; with none, a delegate uses no credential. A credentialed command runs only as `core-env <profile> -- <command>`. Never print, copy or store a value; never run a login command or a command that prints a token; never read the owner's private document or the store; never work in the main checkout or use its env files. A hosted Supabase project is touched only when the brief grants it and names the project; a reset or a rebuild of one only when the brief quotes the coordinator's approval for it (D-37). Nothing that could add to the Supabase bill, ever: no new project or branch, no plan or compute change, no paid add-on (D-37 lists them). Stripe is test mode only: check the mode before the first call and stop on any `livemode: true`. No deployment, promotion, provider setting, email, event, push or pull request, and no write tool of any MCP server, unless the brief quotes the coordinator's approval for that one act. Holding a credential authorizes nothing: the brief does.
10. **Scripts and approvals.** Write a script to a file with your file tools and run it with a short, plain command. Do not pass a long inline script through the shell, a heredoc through `wsl.exe` for one: the harness can hold such a command for an approval that only a person at the screen can give, and you then sit idle while you show as running (D-59).
11. **One gate at a time, and tests under load.** At most one pre-push gate runs on this machine at a time (D-50). A delegate whose brief lets it push looks first for a running gate (`pgrep -f scripts/git/pre-push.mjs`) and waits while there is one. A test file that fails in a full run on a loaded machine is run alone before it is judged, and both results are reported. Since 19 November 2026 the coordinator's push step also takes a lock in WSL, `/tmp/core-prepush-gate.lock`, before it looks, and waits and looks again while another push holds it: two pushes that looked at the same moment could otherwise both start. A review bot on pull request #2724 found that race. The lock closes it only for pushes that take it, so the owner's other programs are to be asked to take it too.

| 4     | WP5 and WP6, in parallel. WP6 runs its four proofs before its baseline migration                                         | WP3 verified                    |

Its fix closed locks altogether: Web Studio no longer asked for lock status and the lock collection's API was closed, so editors lost the notice that someone else is editing, and the take-over. Round 2 had two fresh reviewers (7/10 and 6/10, each: accept after fixes), who found no bypass and no new hole. One blocking defect, a regression of a round 1 fix, which the coordinator confirmed: Payload calls the router with addresses that hold a query only; the slice's router adapter resolved them against the site's origin and not against the page's own address, took the result for a page outside Web Studio, and loaded a new document. So every pause while typing in a list's search box, every sort, every page change and every bulk action reloaded the page, and focus and typed text were lost. No test saw it. Both reviewers, independently, found the cost of closing the locks. Without locks nothing protects two people who edit at once: Payload's save checks the lock and nothing else, pages save themselves on every pause, and navigation and missionary profiles keep no versions, so the last writer wins silently and a change lost there is gone. The plan expects up to five editors at once in a tenant                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Rulings. Old media links get a temporary redirect in the admin app: that app is released before the donor app and no longer answers the old address, so without the redirect images would break in this release and not the next. ## 11. Council reviews

Reviewers are fresh sessions that did not write the work. Each runs in its own worktree under a read-only brief. That boundary is contained, not enforced by the tool, and the coordinator checks each reviewer's worktree for changes afterwards. A score is a reviewer's opinion and replaces no acceptance check. The coordinator adjudicates every finding against the code, the plan and the tests.
